description: Mapillary is a collaborative platform, owned by Meta, for street-level imagery and map data from around the world, holding more than 3 billion street-level images contributed with any kind of camera. Computer vision extracts map features automatically from the images, and the imagery can be browsed in a web explorer, captured with mobile apps and used through developer APIs and GIS integrations such as ArcGIS, so that maps can be updated with details not visible from aerial images. The OpenStreetMap wiki records that Mapillary started as a Swedish startup, was sold to Facebook in June 2020 and publishes its images under CC BY-SA. Coverage: worldwide. Access: free web access and APIs after sign-up. Licence: CC BY-SA images and Mapillary terms. Caveats: coverage and capture dates are uneven, and the provider's licence page could not be read here. Simulation uses are street-level building attributes, facade features and streetscape inventories for exposure and digital twin models. Related records: NUS Global Streetscapes, which draws on Mapillary images.
